transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been taking on way more than I can realistically handle. Projects, workshops, fixing up the studio, client calls… it’s all piling up. At first it felt manageable, but now the deadlines are getting close, and the mortgage is starting to worry me.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been stressed and overwhelmed, but I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless or that I’ve stopped caring about my work. It’s more like there’s too much to keep up with.
Have there been times recently when you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

Yes… lately I’ve had this kind of humming energy in me from the morning on. I keep moving from one thing to the next—rearranging the studio, writing proposals, emailing people, sorting through supplies. Sitting still or being quiet feels almost impossible.
How long have you been feeling this way—this increased energy and constant movement from one task to the next?
It’s been about three months now, I think. It really started after I took on the mortgage for the cottage-studio. Since then I’ve been like this—just constantly going from one thing to the next.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a persistent state of elevated energy, constant activity, and difficulty sitting still for about three months, which began after taking on additional financial responsibility. This raises suspicion for a manic or hypomanic episode, pointing toward Bipolar Disorder (F31.1). Major Depressive Disorder (F32.0/F32.1) is less likely given the absence of depressive symptoms. PTSD (F43.22) is ruled out as there is no indication of trauma or stressor-related symptoms.
